I've written the page around what your data supports. I didn't include the line "our meals will lower your A1C," and I'd recommend against it. Here's why:

- **It's a guarantee your data doesn't support.** 4 of the 14 customers didn't see a drop, and those 14 chose to share their results, so they may not represent everyone else. You also don't know who changed medication during those three months, so the drops can't be credited to the meals alone.
- **It's legally risky.** In the US, the FTC requires solid evidence for health claims in ads. A promise to improve a medical marker needs clinical-level evidence. As a registered dietitian, your license and professional code also put you on the hook for accurate claims.
- **The honest version still sells.** Real numbers from real customers, presented by an RD, are more believable than a blanket promise.

<final_document>
# Lunches and Dinners Planned for Type 2 Diabetes, Delivered Every Sunday

**Cooked meals, planned by a registered dietitian, so you can stop doing the carb math every night.**

Managing type 2 diabetes means thinking about food all day: what you can eat, how much, and whether you have the energy to cook it. We take that work off your plate.

## How it works

Every Sunday we deliver 10 fully cooked lunches and dinners to your door anywhere in the metro area. Heat them up, eat, and get on with your week.

- **45 grams of carbohydrate or less in every meal.** You know what you're getting every time.
- **Every menu is planned by me, a registered dietitian.** These aren't generic "healthy" meals. Each one is built for blood sugar management and to taste good.
- **Real food you'll want to eat.** Balanced meals with enough protein and fiber to keep you full.

## What our customers are seeing

We serve 88 people right now, and 37 of them have been with us for more than six months. People stay because the meals fit their lives.

Some customers have shared their lab results with me. Of the 14 who sent their A1C from before they started and again after three months, 10 saw it go down, with an average drop of 0.6 points. Three stayed about the same, and one went up.

Everyone's body, medications, and routine are different, so I can't promise any specific result. What I can promise is that every meal makes it easier to eat the way your care team recommends, without the planning, shopping, or cooking.

*Our meals are meant to support the care plan from your doctor, not replace it. Talk with your healthcare provider before making changes to how you manage your diabetes.*

## Pricing

**Trial week: $59**
Try a full week of meals before you commit.

**Weekly plan: $129 for 10 meals**
Delivered every Sunday. That's about $12.90 per meal, less than most takeout and with none of the guesswork.

## Start with a trial week

You don't have to change everything at once. Start with one week. See how the meals fit into your routine, how you feel, and whether it makes your days easier.

**[Start Your $59 Trial Week]**

*Questions? Reach out anytime. You'll hear back from me directly.*
</final_document>

Before you publish, please check a few things:

1. **Who the 0.6-point average covers.** I wrote it as the average across all 14 customers. If it's actually the average of only the 10 whose A1C dropped, change the sentence to say so. Otherwise it overstates the result.
2. **Consent.** Make sure the 14 customers agreed to have their results used in your marketing, even as anonymous totals.
3. **The trial conversion rate.** I left out the "1 in 5" figure because it doesn't help persuade a new customer. It's useful for your own planning.

If you'd like a bigger results claim later, consider tracking A1C and medication changes for everyone who agrees to it. That would give you numbers you can stand behind more firmly.
